Send a written objection to the headline only if the journalist asks, because challenging the wording risks losing the coverage altogether.
Reply with the full technical abstract and no example or analogy, so that every statement the public reads is the researcher's own exact wording.

questions.skill: Designing inclusive programs that actually work

questions.answer: Combine structured mentoring and community with clear standards, and evaluate outcomes over several years to see what works.

questions.answer: Assess the research work concretely and on its merits, and explain the teaching load as the reason for the smaller publication record, so the achievements can be compared in context without lowering the standards applied to anyone else.

questions.skill: Designing durable research-practice partnerships
questions.prompt: A research-practice partnership between a university team and a school district has run for two years, but teachers keep returning to old routines once the training workshops end. Which design change best follows current research-practice partnership guidance?
questions.answer: Move from one-off workshops to sustained coaching and joint lesson study tied to the district's own curriculum goals.
choices: Move from one-off workshops to sustained coaching and joint lesson study tied to the district's own curriculum goals.
Add more one-day workshops so teachers hear the new methods more often during the school year.
Publish the partnership's findings in journals so the district can adopt the methods on its own.
Shift the budget toward a larger randomized trial before changing how the work is delivered.

questions.skill: Judging evidence of curricular effectiveness
questions.prompt: A district asks whether a new curriculum actually raises understanding of fractions, and the research team proposes only test-score gains as evidence. What is the strongest addition a mathematician should recommend to judge the change well?
questions.answer: Use classroom observations and student interview tasks, alongside scores, to see how fraction reasoning is actually developing.
choices: Use classroom observations and student interview tasks, alongside scores, to see how fraction reasoning is actually developing.
Rely on the district's end-of-year exam alone, since it is already given every year.
Compare this year's scores with last year's without any other measure of student thinking.

questions.skill: Scaling math circles through volunteer training
questions.prompt: A math circle leader wants volunteer-run circles in many towns to keep their quality as they grow. Which approach best fits how successful circle networks have scaled?
questions.answer: Train volunteers with a shared problem-based curriculum and mentor new leaders, then let each circle adapt problems locally.
choices: Train volunteers with a shared problem-based curriculum and mentor new leaders, then let each circle adapt problems locally.
Require every circle to follow one scripted lesson plan so all sessions match exactly.
Let each circle choose any topics it likes with no shared materials or leader training.
Stop opening new circles and focus only on the original group of talented students.

questions.skill: Reviewing standards with a progression lens
questions.prompt: A state committee revising school mathematics standards asks a research mathematician to review the proposed progression of topics from kindergarten through grade eight. What contribution is most valuable at this stage?
questions.answer: Check that the topics build in a logical order with coherent definitions and no gaps or dead ends, and flag places where a shortcut now creates a misconception later.
choices: Check that the topics build in a logical order with coherent definitions and no gaps or dead ends, and flag places where a shortcut now creates a misconception later.
Rewrite the standards so that the topics most useful for university calculus appear earlier, regardless of how young children actually learn them.
Add several enrichment topics from higher mathematics, such as symmetry groups and infinity, to raise the level of the standards.
Leave the ordering of topics to curriculum vendors and instead write a list of famous open problems to inspire teachers in each grade.

questions.skill: Communicating model assumptions and uncertainty
questions.prompt: An epidemic model used for school-closing decisions has no stated range of validity and is reported to the public as giving exact case forecasts. What is the most important correction a mathematical advisor should demand?
questions.answer: State the model's assumptions, its plausible range, and which outputs are robust enough to act on.
choices: State the model's assumptions, its plausible range, and which outputs are robust enough to act on.
Switch to a more complicated model with more adjustable parameters so forecasts look more precise.
Report only the single best-case scenario so the public is not alarmed by wide ranges.
Withhold the model from decision makers until its predictions match past data perfectly.

questions.skill: Responding to unreliable methods at field scale
questions.prompt: A widely used method in a data-driven field is found to give overstated claims because a common assumption is rarely met in practice. What response best fits field-level stewardship of statistical practice?
questions.answer: Set community standards for checking that assumption and reporting uncertainty, and share worked alternatives.
choices: Set community standards for checking that assumption and reporting uncertainty, and share worked alternatives.
Quietly stop using the method in one's own work and leave the field's habits unchanged.
Ban the method from journals outright, since it is unreliable in at least some settings.
Publish only the cases where the method works, so confidence in it is restored.

questions.skill: Using history to frame modern debates
questions.prompt: In the nineteenth century, mathematicians debated whether existence proofs that do not construct the object were acceptable. How does this episode inform current debates about computer-assisted proofs?
questions.answer: It shows that standards of what counts as proof have shifted over time through argument, so today's debates should examine what understanding the new proofs do and do not provide.
choices: It shows that standards of what counts as proof have shifted over time through argument, so today's debates should examine what understanding the new proofs do and do not provide.
It shows that modern standards are settled once and for all, so computer-assisted proofs need no further discussion.
It shows that only constructive arguments are true mathematics, so any use of a computer is automatically unacceptable.
It shows that history is irrelevant to current practice, since mathematics is a purely cumulative science.

questions.prompt: A public health ministry must decide whether to close schools during an epidemic and asks a mathematician to interpret a model that projects hospitalizations. questions.answer: State which assumptions drive the projections, present the range across the modeling groups and the conditions under which each projection holds, and identify which decisions stay the same across all of the models.

Present all four models as equally valid and let the minister choose among them, since a mathematician should not judge which assumptions are more plausible.
Reply that no useful statement can be made until the modeling groups agree, so the ministry should postpone the decision and wait for a single consensus forecast.
